nodes.name: snapshot

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README and the CLAUDE.md guide to learn what Skilient is: a university-gated platform where Pakistani students prove skills through real project work and turn that proof into a signed, verifiable CV. CLAUDE.md also lists the fixed stack and the hard rules (no AI APIs, no public profiles, RLS everywhere) that shape every later step.

tour.title: Spec and Build Plan
tour.description: The PRD index, the build plan and the decisions log are the source of truth for what to build and why. The build plan splits the work into phases, and the code map in CLAUDE.md follows those phases, so these documents give you the structure for the rest of the tour.

tour.title: App Entry and Gatekeeping
tour.description: Building on the overview, the root layout and proxy.ts are where every request enters the Next.js 16 app. The proxy refreshes the session and applies the gate decision table in lib/auth/gate.ts, which keeps each role (student, recruiter, faculty, official, staff) inside its own portal.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js 16 renames middleware.ts to proxy.ts, and cookies() is now async.

tour.title: Identity in the Database
tour.description: The identity migration holds the signup rules, the profile, and the security-definer functions that run behind public wrappers. Security lives in Postgres with RLS and private-schema functions, so the app layer stays thin. The pgTAP test 00_rls_everywhere fails any public table that lacks RLS.
tour.languageLesson: Row Level Security is default deny in Postgres: a table with RLS and no policy returns no rows to normal roles.

tour.title: Server Actions and Data Reads
tour.description: Every write goes through actionContext, which resolves the user with getUser() and returns a typed ActionResult. rpcAction wraps a single SQL function call and maps SQL errors to typed refusals. Reads use rpc-json, so each page is built from one database call. Together these keep user identity and entitlements out of client hands.

tour.title: UI Shell and Primitives
tour.description: The design-system primitives in components/ui are the most widely imported modules in the repo. lib/nav.ts is the single navigation config behind the sidebar, tablet rail and phone tabs. Together they give every screen one consistent frame.

tour.title: GitHub Evidence Pipeline
tour.description: Students connect GitHub, and a queue-driven worker turns repositories and pull requests into skill evidence. The migration defines the accounts, repos and the pgmq queue, and the worker's logic is written with web APIs only so Node tests can run it. This is the evidence that the CV later signs.

tour.title: Feed, Posts and Ranking
tour.description: The posts migration and the ranked feed migration build the social layer. Posts are the only content type, with no likes or reactions, and the feed score is computed in SQL. The ranking migration scores work, skills, endorsements and credentials into the leaderboard introduced next to it.

tour.title: The Signed Verifiable CV
tour.description: This is the core product. A CV snapshot is built in SQL, then the cv-sign Edge Function signs it with an Ed25519 key kept in Vault. CV control adds share links, revocation and PDF export, and the CV document is rendered by lib/cv/document.ts so recruiters can check it at /verify.

tour.title: Faculty and Recruiter Portals
tour.description: The teacher portal adds supervisors, project ideas and reviews that give the student evidence a second verifier. The recruiter talent migration lets organisations search an anonymised talent index and contact students without exposing names. Both build on the identity and CV steps above.

tour.title: University Portal
tour.description: Universities claim their space, invite admins and manage departments, announcements, events and fairs. The core migration requires two-factor sign-in on every university seat, and its plan stub is later replaced by real billing.

tour.title: Billing and Entitlements
tour.description: The billing core migration defines the entitlement registry and plans, and the lifecycle migration adds checkout, subscriptions and invoices, priced in SQL. lib/billing/registry.ts lists every paid action and its key, and a test fails if a paid action is not registered. This turns the earlier plan stubs into real gating.

tour.title: Staff Operations (/ops)
tour.description: The ops shell migration adds the super-admin role checks, the staff inbox and the audit search. The sanctions and appeals migration adds restrictions that moderators apply and a separate staff member decides on appeal. lib/ops/nav.ts is the one config for the /ops areas, and every staff write is audited.

tour.title: CI and Quality Gates
tour.description: The CI workflow runs typecheck, lint, unit tests, pgTAP and the E2E suite on every pull request. The pgTAP checks include the RLS-everywhere test from step 4. The restore-drill workflow checks that production can be rebuilt from backup.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use on triggers and parallel jobs, and each job runs steps in order.
